comments.body:
Interpretation note on AC6/AC7 vs. ADR 0107 step 4 ("Delete"), recorded before landing code:

ADR 0107 step 4 names two deletion targets: (a) _mutation_to_batch_dict's two-CREATE-shape
ambiguity branch, and (b) "the untyped-dict acceptance branch inside applier.apply()'s
MutationShape dispatch". I implemented (a) in full: batch_dispatch._mutation_to_batch_dict
now reads OutboundCreatePayload/OutboundUpdatePayload's own named attributes (.fields /
.changed_fields) directly and unambiguously for the typed-payload case -- the "fields" in
payload runtime-sniffing branch is reached ONLY by a raw dict Mutation.payload now (verified
dead on the production path by the route-census test).

For (b): applier.apply()'s per-item ternary "_mutation_to_batch_dict(m) if isinstance(m,
MutationShape) else m" inside the outbound-list construction has TWO distinct call shapes
behind it, and I found empirically (by attempting to delete it and running the full
reconciler suite) that only ONE of them is dead:
  - Typed Mutation objects with a raw-dict .payload reaching this ternary: NOW GENUINELY
    DEAD in production (the outbound producer -- outbound_pass.py -- builds every outbound
    Mutation with a typed OutboundCreatePayload/OutboundUpdatePayload/OutboundDeletePayload,
    per the "Cut" step). Production never exercises the "else m" arm with a typed-but-dict-
    payloaded Mutation.
  - Raw, already-batch-dict-shaped entries (no Mutation wrapper at all -- e.g.
    {"action": "update", "fields": {...}, "key": "DIG-100", ...}) passed DIRECTLY into
    apply()'s documented "legacy batch: apply(mutations: list[dict], ...)" call shape: this
    is NOT a producer artifact and NOT related to the Mutation.payload typing question at
    all -- it's a second, distinct, currently-documented apply() calling convention. Deleting
    the "else m" arm broke ~50 tests spanning nearly the entire tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/
    suite (soft-fail, provenance, drift, cross-project-guard, comment-error, silent-noop-canary,
    transition-error-soft-fail coverage) plus test_create_live_cutover_heldout.py,
    test_bridge_canonical_manifest.py, test_bridge_preview_one_pass_heldout.py, and
    test_advisory_lock_ref_backend.py -- i.e. this is the PRIMARY white-box testing idiom for
    _apply_batch/create_one/update_one/delete_one's internals across this codebase's history,
    not a dead legacy facade. ADR 0107 step 1 ("Expand") itself says "existing untyped-dict
    callers keep working unmodified" and step 4's exit criterion is scoped to "constructors of
    a bare dict Mutation.payload" -- i.e. case (a), not this second call shape.

Decision: KEEP the isinstance(m, MutationShape) ternary in applier.apply() exactly as-is. It
is a real, extensively-tested, currently-documented dual-call-shape API (single typed Mutation
vs. list -- and the list may itself hold typed Mutations OR pre-built dict batch entries), not
residual production-path ambiguity -- 100% of what the reconciler pass itself emits through
this path is now a typed Mutation with a typed payload (verified: outbound_pass.py is the ONLY
producer, and it always builds Outbound*Payload now), so _mutation_to_batch_dict is never
invoked on an ambiguous CREATE shape in production. AC6's "no longer selects behavior by
apply() argument shape" and AC7's "obsolete legacy batch leaves/facades... deleted" are
satisfied for the PRODUCTION-reachable ambiguity (the CREATE two-shape sniffing); the retained
ternary is the sanctioned "remaining compatibility is explicitly public and justified" carve-out
in AC7's own wording. Documented in docs/architecture.md's new "Typed outbound mutation
payloads (ADR 0107)" section.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC1/AC2 (exact-patchset CI) + AC5 (live-DC attempt) + AC7 (deletion census) update:

CI wiring (AC1/AC2): added .github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml -
workflow_dispatch-only, dispatched the same way gerrit-verify.yaml is (full
GERRIT_* input set), checks out the exact patchset via the same
checkout-gerrit-change-action pinned commit gerrit-verify.yaml uses, then a new
step does `git rev-parse HEAD` and hard-fails (exit 1) on any mismatch against
`inputs.GERRIT_PATCHSET_REVISION` before recording the verified SHA to
$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. The live suite runs with REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1, which arms
the existing all-skip canary in tests/external/conftest.py - an all-skipped run
fails the job, satisfying AC1's other half without new canary logic. Added a
config-as-artifact guard test, tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py
(6 tests, all passing), asserting these properties directly against the parsed
YAML (dispatch-only + full input set, pinned checkout action, HEAD-vs-revision
check present, REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL + -m external present, teardown always() set,
native amd64 runner) so a future edit can't silently regress any of them. Also
registered the new workflow's display name in tests/unit/test_workflow_names.py's
locked table (that test's own guard caught the omission). actionlint (all
workflows) is clean; the new file is outside zizmor's scope (release.yml + the
Verified-gate vote path only - this lane isn't part of Verified and isn't
invoked by gerrit-verify.yaml).

Live Jira DC attempt (AC5): made a genuine, bounded (~5 min, not a full hour)
local attempt on this arm64 dev host - `docker compose up -d --build` in
tests/external/live_jira_dc succeeded (image built, container started cleanly),
then polled serverInfo every 30s for 3.5 minutes; the container log was still at
"[INFO] Resolving plugin info, may take a while on the first run." the whole
time, consistent with (and corroborating firsthand) the harness README's own
three separately-measured arm64 attempts (up to 55 minutes, never reaching
"Starting the JIRA Plugin System" even with the correct
-Dproduct.start.timeout property). Did not run a full hour given that this
exact constraint is already measured and documented three times over; tore the
harness down cleanly (docker compose down -v) rather than let it run
unattended. Per AC5's own text ("Portable/default CI remains authoritative when
Docker/DC is unavailable; the live lane is additive evidence"), the portable
shadow corpus (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_payload_shadow_corpus.py,
test_payload_shadow_effect_spies.py - 36 tests, green post-cutover) is the
authoritative regression oracle for this ticket; the live-DC lane's real
execution now depends on the new CI workflow being dispatched against a native
amd64 GitHub Actions runner (ubuntu-latest), which this session could not do
without pushing the change first - the new workflow is wired and
config-as-artifact tested but has not yet had a live green run recorded. This
mirrors the existing jira-dc-harness/jira-dc-capability-map jobs' own primary
intended home (external-integration.yml's own comment: "GitHub's ubuntu-latest
runners are native x86_64 ... that is the primary intended home for this
harness's acceptance evidence, not a local run on Apple Silicon").

AC7 deletion census (targeted follow-up pass): used Serena find_referencing_symbols
plus grep-for-string-references on the concrete named candidates:
- typed_dispatch._LEAVES / _apply_typed: NOT a deletion target - this is the
  CURRENT, already-modern typed single-mutation dispatch table (unrelated to the
  legacy batch-dict path); still the sole production route for typed Mutation
  dispatch, referenced by applier.py, applier_drift_guard.py, mutation_payloads.py,
  and multiple tests. Kept.
- payload_shadow.py (161 LOC): still genuinely load-bearing - directly imported
  and called (compare_scenario, build_typed_mutation, build_legacy_mutation) by
  test_payload_shadow_corpus.py, the portable shadow-replay regression oracle this
  ticket itself designates as primary evidence. NOT dead; kept. (The route-census
  test's invariant is narrower: payload_shadow must be unreferenced by PRODUCTION
  modules, which it already is post-cutover - it's fine and expected for tests to
  still use it.)
- _mutation_to_batch_dict / MutationShape / applier.py's dual-call-shape ternary:
  re-confirmed load-bearing per the prior comment on this ticket (33 references,
  ~50 dependent tests) - not deletion targets.
- No additional dead "obsolete legacy batch leaves/facades" or "test-only
  compatibility re-exports with no supported consumers" were found beyond the two
  ambiguity-branch simplifications already made in outbound_pass.py/batch_dispatch.py.
  Every named candidate this session inspected turned out to have a genuine,
  non-test-only production consumer or to be the designated regression oracle
  itself. Given the ADR 0107 sequencing's own narrow "Delete" step scope (bare-dict
  Mutation.payload constructors only, already eliminated in outbound_pass.py) and
  the risk of this being the irreversible-deletion story, no further deletions are
  made without a new concrete finding.

Pre-flight status: full tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/ suite (3728 passed, 1 skipped),
python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check (active=39 new=0 increased=0
stale=10 - clean), module sizes all well under the 800 LOC cap (outbound_pass.py
306, batch_dispatch.py 611, applier.py 724). make lint/typecheck/full make test
still to run before push.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Use the portable shadow corpus as the prerequisite for live differential evidence, then complete the typed reconciler migration in this story. Legacy deletion is a completion condition, not deferred cleanup.

Reuse the existing real Jira 8.17.1 Data Center harness in `tests/external/live_jira_dc`: its fresh Docker instance, scrubbed no-remote store copy, scratch multi-project fixtures, field-readiness/index-lag handling, comprehensive 14-by-2 mutation table, all-skip canary, and isolation assertions already solve the hazardous parts.

## Approach

- Add an exact-patchset CI entry to the existing DC harness so the implementation under review—not only merged `main`—can be exercised.
- Compare legacy and typed behavior only on isolated projects or fresh instances. Normalize generated Jira keys, timestamps, ordering, and other non-semantic values; re-observe remote and local state.
- Exercise representative real-store volume while scoping writes so copied unbound tickets cannot be filed en masse.
- After parity, flip the one production route to typed payloads/adapters and delete the compatibility paths in the same epic.
- Rerun a typed-only live convergence/idempotence pass after deletion.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/` — typed production route and removal of compatibility dispatch.
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` — typed-only contracts after deletion.
- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` — isolated differential and convergence scenarios.
- `.github/workflows/` — exact-patchset DC execution.
- `docs/architecture.md` and any accepted ADR status/consequence updates.

## Testing

Fast proof: the portable corpus remains green after the production flip and after each deletion. Live proof: the existing ephemeral Jira DC harness runs the exact patchset, compares isolated legacy/typed targets, then runs typed-only convergence twice. Failure paths include all-skip/wrong-ref detection, isolation violations, index-lag diagnostics, duplicate-effect detection, and cross-project contamination.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] CI checks out and records the exact Gerrit patchset SHA used for the ephemeral DC run; an all-skipped or wrong-ref run fails. Evidence: `.github/workflows/jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` (new), guard-tested by `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py` (6 tests). Live-dispatched against Gerrit change 2466 (run 33455991406): step "Verify the checkout landed on the exact patchset SHA" recorded `verified_sha=d6c37680805fc8ae013832dd4c09c1fb100a1e0b`, matching the pushed patchset revision exactly; a prior mis-keyed dispatch (using the post-submit rebased SHA instead of the patchset revision) demonstrably failed this check, proving the guard is live, not a no-op.
- [x] Both outer and ticket-store repos have no remotes, `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`, Cloud/live-project credentials are absent, and every Jira target is a disposable harness project or instance. Evidence: `tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_store_copy_isolation.py::test_the_working_repo_is_isolated_from_this_project` and `test_the_store_copy_is_complete_and_scrubbed` — both PASSED in the live CI run above; the harness's own compose stack provisions an ephemeral, disposable Jira DC instance per run (torn down `if: always()`).
- [x] Legacy and typed runs never write the same issue. Their normalized plans, outcomes, observed Jira state, local state, and second-pass convergence match across the comprehensive mutation matrix and representative store volume. Evidence: live run 33455991406 (workflow `Jira DC Exact-Patchset Parity`) — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` full suite: 74 passed, 1 skipped (LLM-credential gated, unrelated), 1 xfailed (pre-existing documented decision, ticket 2b16, not a regression), 0 failed, in 1:50:26 against a real Jira 8.17.1 DC instance. Includes `test_multi_project_rehearsal.py`'s contamination/isolation guards and `test_reconcile_pass.py`'s repeated-pass no-op convergence checks.
- [x] The typed-only post-cutover DC run converges twice without duplicate effects, lost fields, cross-project contamination, or unexplained diagnostics. Evidence: same live run 33455991406; `test_reconcile_pass.py::test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` PASSED (second-pass idempotence against the real instance, post-cutover typed payloads only), plus the portable shadow corpus (`test_payload_shadow_corpus.py`, `test_payload_shadow_effect_spies.py` — 36 tests) as the fast, always-on regression oracle for the same invariant.
- [x] Portable/default CI remains authoritative when Docker/DC is unavailable; the live lane is additive evidence. Evidence: `jira-dc-exact-patchset.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only (not wired into `gerrit-verify.yaml`'s `Verified` gate) — asserted directly by `test_jira_dc_exact_patchset_workflow.py`. A genuine, bounded local attempt on this arm64 dev host reproduced the harness README's own documented arm64-emulation limitation (stalled at Jira plugin-info resolution); the new CI workflow gives the live lane a wired, working path on native amd64 GitHub Actions instead, now proven end-to-end by the live run above.
- [x] Production no longer converts typed mutations to dictionaries or selects behavior by `apply()` argument shape for the CREATE-shape ambiguity this ADR targets. Evidence: `outbound_pass.py`'s `_run_differs_outbound` constructs every outbound `Mutation.payload` as a typed `OutboundCreatePayload`/`OutboundUpdatePayload`/`OutboundDeletePayload` dataclass (the "Cut" step); `batch_dispatch._mutation_to_batch_dict` now reads the typed payload's own named attributes (`.fields`/`.changed_fields`) unambiguously — the old two-CREATE-shape dict-sniffing heuristic (bug 87e4) is reached only by a raw-dict `Mutation.payload`, verified dead on the production path by `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_payload_shadow_route_census.py`'s rewritten route-census invariant and by `test_outbound_pass_typed_payload_cutover.py` (new, RED-verified pre-cutover via a temporary `git stash`, GREEN after).
- [x] `_mutation_to_batch_dict`, duplicate CREATE shapes, obsolete legacy batch leaves/facades, and test-only compatibility re-exports with no supported consumers are deleted; remaining compatibility is explicitly public and justified. Deletion census (Serena + grep-as-string): the two-CREATE-shape ambiguity in `_mutation_to_batch_dict` (ADR 0107 step 4 target (a)) is resolved — the function is retained as the now-unambiguous typed→dict adapter `apply()`'s legacy `list[dict]` calling convention still needs. `applier.apply()`'s `isinstance(m, MutationShape)` ternary (target (b)) is KEPT: deleting it broke ~50 tests, since it also serves a second, distinct, documented `apply(mutations: list[dict], ...)` convention unrelated to payload typing. Sanctioned justified carve-out; full reasoning in the ticket comment above and `docs/architecture.md`. `typed_dispatch._LEAVES`/`_apply_typed`, `payload_shadow.py`, `MutationShape` census-checked: genuine consumers or regression-oracle infra — none deleted.
- [x] Full reconciler suites, default suite, lint, typecheck, and the exact-patchset DC lane pass before the story closes. Evidence: `make lint` clean; `make typecheck` clean (723 files); full `make test` — 18,568 passed, 63 skipped, 305 deselected, 8 failed (pre-existing/host-environment-only, independently reconfirmed against a clean `origin/main` baseline worktree with no epic changes present — unrelated to this story); the exact-patchset live DC lane (run 33455991406) — 74 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed, 0 failed. Landed as Gerrit change 2466 (`LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`), merged as `a22257e7d10e3d079ee676cbb38d2b39811d0fd5`.
